clue.text: Those attending university are inside — one's likely to be rich

indicators.note: the word before it is said to sit inside the rest, so it is placed within the other letters

parts.note: a gate is the number of people attending a match
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Students turning up to university are said to be wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The are (100 square metres) goes inside GATE plus U to give GATEAU. 'Are' looks like a verb but is the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gâteau is a cream-laden cake, the kind of dessert described as very rich.

clue.text: We object over a guest? That's not it, boss

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the object form of the pronoun we

indicators.note: says the two letters spelling it must be taken out of the preceding word

parts.note: as in five pounds a head, per head

explanation.surface: We complain about a visitor; the boss replies that's not the point.
explanation.walkthrough: US reversed, PER, then VISITOR without IT: SU+PER+VISOR. 'A' meaning per is a common trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor is the person in charge who oversees workers, a boss.

clue.text: Cycling country is welcoming fellow countrymen

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other
going round in a cycle, the final letter moves round to the front

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A cycling-mad nation is warmly receiving its own compatriots.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling here moves a word's last letter round to its front. 'Fellow' looks like part of the definition, but only 'countrymen' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanis are natives of Afghanistan, so they are fellow countrymen of one another.

clue.text: Girl with old man's plain

parts.note: pa is father, the old man; add the possessive S

explanation.surface: A young woman is accompanied by her father's rather ordinary looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective about the father but is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grassland plains of South America.

clue.text: Support Hungary's financial centre — why I think it'll happen

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
EC is the postcode of the City of London
the letter Y is said the same as why

explanation.surface: Someone backs Budapest as a money hub and explains their confident forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the City, Britain's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophecy is a prediction, a statement that something is going to happen.

clue.text: Fellow is hiding right-wing prejudice

indicators.note: something hidden is kept inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a dry is a hardline right-wing Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: A man is concealing his right-wing bias.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'dry' is a hardline Thatcherite Tory, as opposed to a 'wet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Misandry is hatred of or bias against men, a particular form of prejudice.

clue.text: Repeatedly pushed against having meal with my boss

parts.note: a buffet is a self-service meal
ED is short for editor, the boss on a newspaper

explanation.surface: An office worker is jostled at a lunch spread alongside the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Guardian, 'my boss' for the setter is the crossword editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be buffeted is to be struck again and again, as by wind or waves.

clue.text: Politician getting zero in test

indicators.note: placing one thing in another means it goes inside it

explanation.surface: A politician scores nothing in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, hence a politician.

clue.text: I should have seen that about Special's money

indicators.note: something placed about another surrounds it, so it wraps the next piece

parts.note: Homer Simpson's exclamation of annoyance at missing the obvious
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Someone kicks themselves for missing something about a Special's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: D'OH wraps S. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal British slang for cash, money.

clue.text: Teacher assessors kicked out — there's a little fantasy for you

indicators.text: there's a little fantasy for you
indicators.note: this phrase swaps one letter for another, putting a small bit of the word fantasy where the letter u stood

parts.note: a little of the word: its first letter

explanation.surface: School inspectors get sacked, and someone sneers that it's wishful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For you' is read as 'for U': swap the U in OUSTED for F to give OFSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofsted is the English body that inspects schools and assesses teaching standards.

clue.text: Chickens on skewers?

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
horns are what skewer a matador

explanation.surface: Poultry threaded on kebab sticks, ready for the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side of the field is also called the leg side, so 'on' can give LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leghorn is a breed of domestic chicken named after the Italian port of Livorno.

clue.text: One nervous replaying after home draw

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for home, as in fixture lists

indicators.note: playing something again in a new way suggests these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious player faces a replay after a draw at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The football setting suggests a fixture, but 'draw' is the definition and 'home' gives only H.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Honours even' is the idiom for a contest ending level, with neither side ahead: a draw.

clue.text: After vacant house to rent round King's Head (where the neighbours aren't friendly)

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece, enclosing it
something rent is torn apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
a vacant word is emptied of its middle, so only its outside letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of the word

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Looking for a house to let near a pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rental and a pub; 'vacant' empties After to AR, and 'rent' means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: South Korea borders hostile North Korea, so its neighbours are anything but friendly.

clue.text: Spirited females allow men only to speak

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: allowing only men means barring the shes, the women

explanation.surface: Feisty women permit only men to address the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited females' sounds like lively women, but means female spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is a female spirit of Irish folklore whose wail foretells a death.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing Dawn shortly about to bale out

indicators.note: turned about, the shortened word is read backwards
cut short, the word loses its final letter
knocked out of shape, these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A useless person named Dawn is about to jump from a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a name; it is SUNUP, docked and reversed to UNUS, then BALE rearranged as ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusable is of no use at all, good for nothing.

clue.text: Animal cry of dissatisfaction from Johnson's latest heard

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: Carrie is Boris Johnson's latest wife
the jeer of a disgruntled crowd

explanation.surface: A jeer from the latest arrival in Johnson's circle is overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrie Johnson is the third wife of former UK prime minister Boris Johnson; 'latest' means most recent spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large wild deer.

clue.text: Those having fun on the river catching large fish

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so it ends up inside

parts.words: Those having fun on the river

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: People enjoying a boat trip land a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface catches a large fish; really L is caught. Bloaters are a British food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring cured by salting and light smoking, so a fish.

clue.text: Cross-country with Mark — keep going

indicators.note: crossing over to the other side, the word ends up facing back the other way

explanation.surface: A cross-country runner called Mark is urged to keep running.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-country reads as one running term, but Cross works on country alone, and Mark is no runner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain it, keep it up.

clue.text: Hussies' room? Naughty, naughty!

indicators.note: badly behaved letters do not stay in order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tut-tutting look into a bedroom for brazen women.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Naughty' rearranges; the second, with its exclamation, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ooh er, missus!' is a British catchphrase from comic innuendo, a mock-shocked cry at something saucy.

clue.text: Reptile again running round university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece
letters set running scatter and come back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A lizard is loose again, circling the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, a reptile.

clue.text: Women missed out on pay for a long time

indicators.note: something missed out is left off, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Women went without proper pay for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a protest about unequal pay; 'for' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal plural noun meaning a very long period.

clue.text: Radical left supporting high-flier Johnson?

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the piece before this word goes below the one after

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A left-wing extremist backs the high-flying politician Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts L below AMY. Amy Johnson flew solo from England to Australia in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl is a chemical radical, the pentyl group C5H11, not a political extremist.

clue.text: Simple-minded lead in movie, one hampered by fashion sense

parts.note: Forrest Gump, the simple-minded hero of the film

indicators.note: something hampered is hemmed in, so it sits inside what hampers it

explanation.surface: A dim-witted film star, held back by style, still shows good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is practical common sense and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Wonderful to be leading in National

indicators.note: placed in another word, these letters go inside it

parts.note: a Serb is a national of Serbia
a team that is up is ahead, leading

explanation.surface: Leading in the Grand National would be fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital N suggests the horse race; here National is a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent or magnificent, a synonym of wonderful.

clue.text: Son cleared over fifty spent freely

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: lying over something covers it, so it ends up inside

explanation.surface: A son, freed of his debts past fifty, went on a spending spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money lavishly and extravagantly.

clue.text: Legendary monster, one advancing, actually existing!

indicators.note: advancing moves a letter out of its place and forward to the front

explanation.surface: The Loch Ness monster turns out to be real after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in NESSIE moves forward to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In esse is Latin for in actual being, describing something that really exists.
